U2 scoping findings -- attempted U2 (graded mode affordance + Phase-C percussion enactment, consolidation_v1.md section 4) this session, immediately after U1/ED-PC-0010 landed and unblocked it. Found U2's one-line spec ('drop cut_factor 0.45 floor, per-primitive gates MODE_EDGE_MIN/MODE_TIP_MIN/MODE_PERC_MIN, wire geo[thrust], drop percussion blunt self-gate, fix the 8.0 cap/mace-pin inversion') materially underspecified for a safe implementation -- the missing source plan (A: /root/.claude/plans/fuzzy-toasting-wombat.md, not present in this environment) evidently carried detail consolidation_v1.md's summary table did not preserve. THREE new findings, each requiring its own Jordan-reviewed default before U2 can safely land (none implemented this pass -- no risky guess committed to engine code):

(1) PERCUSSION SELF-GATE REMOVAL PRODUCES A SEVERE BALANCE REGRESSION, NOT 'ships weak' (JD-4's own framing). Measured directly: naively dropping weapon_physics.percussion_authority's head-not-blunt-returns-zero gate and letting every weapon's own mass*PoB_frac*energy_credit feed the existing PERC_SCALE=9.5/PERC_EXP=0.30 formula gives greatsword=6.12, katana=6.26, longsword=5.77 -- comparable to or exceeding poleaxe's own 7.48 and close to mace's 8.0 cap. Root cause: PERC_SCALE/PERC_EXP were fit ONLY against dedicated blunt weapons (whose entire forward mass IS the striking surface); a sword's percussion-capable mass is specifically its small rear pommel, not its whole blade+PoB -- the existing whole-weapon formula has no way to distinguish these cases. JD-4's 'ships weak' default cannot be honored by a bare self-gate removal; a genuinely NEW pommel-specific percussion sub-model (grounded per this repo's own combat-grounding-methodology: derive from the pommel's own mass_kg/x_m via percussion_element_authority, not the whole-weapon formula) is needed first. NOT implemented.

(2) weapon_physics.thrust_factor (geometry.py) carries its OWN undocumented floor bug, structurally identical to cut_factor's already-flagged 0.45 floor: its formula (0.35 + 0.65*point_concentration) times a cross_section term never reaches 0 even at point_concentration=0 (a broad, pointless face). Measured: mace (pc=0.02, pure blunt face) scores thrust=0.34; staff scores 0.31 -- both nontrivial 'thrust' readings for weapons with no point at all, purely from their rigid cross_section. This forces any MODE_TIP_MIN choice into an uncomfortably narrow band (0.34-0.37) to satisfy the plan's own test_mace_staff_no_thrust (must exclude mace 0.34/staff 0.31) AND test_greatsword_katana_sabre_afford_thrust (must include sabre, whose thrust=0.37 clears that same window by only 0.03) -- a fragile margin this repo's own anti-sim-fit principle (Jordan memory: combat-grounding-methodology) warns against accepting silently. Proposed default (not applied): drop thrust_factor's own floor the same way U2 already drops cut_factor's, widening the margin -- but this is an ADDITIONAL formula change beyond consolidation_v1's literal text and needs the same sign-off as JD-1 was, not a silent bundle.

(3) The graded-affordance change (decoupling element_afforded's per-mode gating from the head category) has a MUCH wider blast radius than the plan's 5 named acceptance tests. Verified directly: test_combat_invariants.py already carries exact-set assertions for composite weapons (test_afforded_heads_emerge_from_phase_b2_mode_elements: ji=={point,curved_cut}, guisarme=={cut_thrust,point}, voulge, bec_de_corbin, lucerne_hammer, goedendag, poleaxe) that a straightforward head-independent secondary cut/point check WOULD break -- e.g. ji's point-tokened spearhead element carries edge_keenness=0.40 in its own per-mode_element geometry, comfortably clearing a MODE_EDGE_MIN~=0.15 floor and adding a THIRD 'cut' token to a set the existing test pins at exactly two. Landing U2 correctly requires re-deriving the expected new set for every composite weapon in the roster (the same rigor as a fixture regeneration, but with no existing 'right answer' to check against), not just the 5 single-mode weapons the plan names.

RECOMMENDATION: resolve (1) and (2) as their own Jordan-reviewed forks (proposed as JD-9 and JD-10 respectively, extending consolidation_v1.md section 6) before attempting U2's implementation; (3) is a scope/effort note for whoever implements U2, not a design fork. NOTHING in geometry.py/systems.py/weapon_physics.py was changed this session -- all three findings were verified by direct interactive measurement against the live post-U1 tree, not applied.

Thrust authority (point-to-hand lever) — the grounding for the half-sword-wins-at-heavy outcome (RBNI register item PC-5) and the armour-conditional correction of G4 reach-dominance. Adds core.thrust_authority(head_len) = clamp(THRUST_LEVER_REF/head_len, THRUST_LEVER_FLOOR, 1.0) (REF=0.55 m, FLOOR=0.30). PHYSICS: driving a point into a harness gap is a pommel-backed SHORT-LEVER act (Fiore/Talhoffer half-sword; the rondel/misericorde to the visor/armpit) — a short point-to-controlling-hand distance (dagger head_len 0.21, half-sworded longsword 0.42) presses the point home behind body-mass; a long reach-thrust at extension (spear 1.65, yari 1.86) delivers the same point but cannot back it the same way. SCOPE (surgical): thrust_auth scales the GAP-PRESS term ONLY — core._transmit('puncture') gap term (GAP_EXPOSURE*gap_prec*thrust_auth) and adef_cap's point / cut_thrust gap-thrust (ADEF_POINT*gap*tauth). The THROUGH-MATERIAL term (a thrust that lands on flesh/cloth) is UNTOUCHED, so reach weapons stay lethal vs soft targets (spear vs light 85->82%); the blunt/percussion armour-defeat path (swung beak/spike: bec_de_corbin, poleaxe) is UNTOUCHED (a swung spike is not a static pommel-press). Threaded through coupling/damage/strike (from the SELECTED weapon record's head_len — the half-sword swap already carries the short-lever form's own head_len) and select_mode's greedy comparator. RESULTS (seeded winrate): longsword-half-sword vs arming, both heavy 38%->73% (the liability->advantage flip); LS unarmoured/light vs arming-heavy still loses 11-13% (correctly should not half-sword); spear vs arming ladder none 87/light 80/medium 63/HEAVY 28% (was flat ~85%) — reach decays with armour; yari heavy 21%; guisarme heavy 49% (versatile, contests); poleaxe heavy 97% (dedicated armour-defeater still dominates); dagger vs arming heavy 72%->93% (the close-in armour-killer). CONSEQUENCE (loud, per ED-1094): overturns THREE pre-PC-5 balance invariants that encoded UNIFORM plate-defeat — test_reach_class_beats_arming_not_inverted (reach no longer beats arming at HEAVY for pure-point weapons — the intended G4 correction), test_heavy_mirror_fair_and_decisive (an arming-sword/spear plate mirror now STALEMATES, decided<40% — the historical why-men-at-arms-wrestled, while dagger/mace/poleaxe mirrors stay decisive), and test_use_mode_selection_emerges_from_primitives (changer set: +estoc/flamberge/changdao/odachi thrust-blades gaining armour-conditional half-sword thrust, extending the ED-PC-0011 pattern; -bec_de_corbin/voulge routed off a static-thrust label onto their percussion/versatile path, outcome preserved 91%/63% at heavy). Half-sword roster expansion to the attested ricassos (RBNI register item PC-2, per JD-3 / Jordan's ricasso ruling). U9 — JOINT RECALIBRATION + CAPSTONE (R3 consolidation_v1.md §6 U9, the LAST slice of the U0→U9 sequence; RBNI item PC-6). U9's charter: flip the U3/U5/U7 constants, ablation-gate every lever, cut any lever that doesn't move outcomes beyond noise. Ablation method: workbench/balance.py winrate matrix, each constant flipped in isolation on its BEST-CASE matchup, noise floor ~±4pp at n∈{350,500}, multi-seed {3,5,7,11} confirmation. RESULT: no lever robustly clears the noise floor even in its own best case (best was BIND_SPINE +3.5pp, decays to noise on re-seed). The one that looked live at low-N single-seed (CHOKE_THRUST spear-vs-arming −4.7/−5.3/−7.6pp) COLLAPSED to seed-noise at higher N (mean −0.1..−1.9pp, signs flip) — the earlier reading was seed cherry-picking, corrected here (the U9 adversarial pass: the producer's own promising result did not survive the critic). VERDICT: cut NOTHING (the six mechanisms are grounded HEMA/physics facts, situational not aggregate — winrate is the wrong instrument for a lever that decides one bind/grab/read in twenty fights — live-not-dead by their unit tests, and byte-identical so zero cost to retain), activate NOTHING; re-charter activation as scenario-specific micro-calibration (out of U9 scope). HELD-BACK HARD DESIGN CALL (needs_jordan, ED-1094 — NOT bundled): activating CHOKE_THRUST (lever 5) independently breaks the RATIFIED grip-invariant-thrust first principle (test_combat_choke.py::test_thrust_grip_invariant_at_k_zero: an axial point-head thrust is grip-invariant, phi_grip==1.0 at every grip). Options for Jordan: (a) hold the principle, CHOKE_THRUST_K stays 0 permanently (recommended default — §2.3 shows it moves no aggregate balance anyway); (b) admit a shallow floored choke exception (≤25% loss, choked head-heavy pole only), re-baselining the invariant to un-choked grips. No code rides on the ruling either way (lever at K=0). Closes the U0→U9 sequence: 7 grounded byte-identical slices (PC-1/PC-2/PC-4/PC-5, U3, U5, U7) + this capstone; net engine-balance effect zero by design. description: A7a CHANNEL 1 — NATIVE EDGE QUALITY IS FINALLY CONSUMED (M6, the ⛎1 direction resolved by Jordan's live authorization + physical grounding, 2026-07-29). DEFECT: core.coupling scaled a cut by its derived edge quality ONLY for the bare 'cut' token, which core.py's own comment records "is NEVER a weapon's own native head" (it is the incidental-edge token a rapier or mace picks up). The two NATIVE cut heads, curved_cut (12) and straight_cut (4), were never scaled at all: 16 weapons, 31% of the roster, coupled identically regardless of their edge. Worse, the scaling that DID exist could not have graded them — the native cut-eff population runs 0.710 (hook_sword) to 1.330 (shamshir), entirely ABOVE CUT_AUTH_REF=0.70, so min(1.0, eff/CUT_AUTH_REF) is identically 1.000 for all 16. The defect register's own proposed fix WAS that expression and is provably a NO-OP; this was re-derived independently before building. WHY THIS WAS THE TOP BALANCE DEFECT: the four keenest edges in the game were four of the five worst performers in the only context they exist for. Measured against the civilian sidearm field (Jordan's carry ruling, same day): shamshir eff 1.330 -> 41.5%, pulwar 1.240 -> 35.5% (last), sabre 1.180 -> 38.2%, scimitar 1.220 -> 47.9%, against rapier (a POINT) at 80.6%. THE FORM, grounded by Jordan not chosen by me: "cutters need to be excellent in contexts where they can CUT ie unarmoured and light armour" + "the curve extends the amount of cutting edge with which to do damage". The second is ALREADY derived — geometry.cut_factor = edge_keenness*(1+0.45*tanh(2*curvature)) adds up to +45% for curvature — and was discarded downstream, so this batch INVENTS NO QUANTITY, it stops a derived one being thrown away. New CUT_REF_NATIVE=1.00, anchored on the KATANA (derived cut_factor exactly 1.00), following the module's own named-weapon precedent (CUT_AUTH_REF<-hook_sword, THRUST_AUTH_REF<-bear_spear, PERC_AUTH_REF_SOFT<-weakest hammer). NON-SATURATING, which is what forced the ⛎1 direction: a cap can only ever PENALISE, so re-anchoring min(1.0,...) could not have helped a population that is already losing. The benefit is gated on the existing _transmit('shear',mat) normalised (none 1.000/cloth 0.618/mail 0.277/plate 0.193) — no new constant, the gate IS the owned resist table; the PENALTY is ungated, because a poor edge is poor everywhere. A second reference rather than a re-anchor because the two populations do not overlap: the incidental token's eff runs 0.02-0.50, genuinely below 0.70, and its own grading is correct and untouched. MEASURED RESULT — correct direction, insufficient magnitude, reported as such: scimitar +6.1pp, pulwar +4.7, shamshir +2.8, sabre +2.3; falchion -5.2, arming -1.9. Civilian sidearm spread 45.1 -> 40.6pp. **THE RAPIER IS UNTOUCHED at 80.8% and remains a 26pp outlier** — it is a POINT weapon, so cut grading cannot reach it. A7a was a real defect and is fixed; it is NOT the cause of the rapier problem, and this batch does not claim to have solved the civilian field. DISCLOSED, NOT TUNED (needs_jordan): the penalty side flips two selections at 'none' — greatsword (eff 0.80) and hook_sword (eff 0.71), the two lowest native cut effs, now prefer their point unarmoured. A greatsword preferring the point unarmoured is questionable feel; it is a consequence of the katana anchor de-rating everything beneath it, and the anchor choice is Jordan's to confirm or move. description: CLOSE-QUARTERS UNWIELDINESS: A FIAT GATE REPLACED BY A DERIVATION (Jordan, 2026-07-29: "that looks like fiat... you can't do a full thrust or swing one foot away holding a rapier... unwieldiness would be a function purely derived from things like shaft length, hand position on shaft, point of balance, head weight"). DEFECT: close_unwieldiness's own docstring claimed "DERIVED from its reach... pure morphology", but it computed max(0, reach_base(c) - CLOSE_REACH_REF) with CLOSE_REACH_REF=6.5. reach_base is L0 + REACH_GEOM_SCALE*forward_extent + reach_adj, and L0=4.0 IS THE FIGHTER'S OWN ARM — so the threshold sat on a scale where 4.0 is the body, and the implied weapon threshold was (6.5-4.0)/2.1167 = 1.18 m of FORWARD EXTENT before a weapon was unwieldy in the close at all. A close/grapple happens near 0.45 m, so the gate was ~3x too permissive AND, being a threshold, produced a CLIFF. Measured: EVERY one-handed sword paid exactly 0.0000 (dagger 0.21 m, arming 0.72, rapier 0.96, longsword 0.94); only estoc 1.30 / spear 1.79 / guandao 2.17 crossed it. WHY IT MATTERED: reach has FOUR benefit channels and this was its ONLY cost, so length was a FREE attribute for anything sword-length. FIX: max(0, forward_extent(grip) - CLOSE_ENGAGE_M), in honest metres, continuous from zero. It was also measured unusable raw: I_g spans ~1000x across the roster, so a linear inertia multiplier reads guandao 48.9 against its prior 2.10 — the same linear-vs-compressed error this session already made once in the bind. Polearms land near their prior values (spear 1.344 vs 1.297, guandao 1.725 vs 2.104), so POLE_CLOSE_K and CHOKE_DRIVE_REF were NOT re-anchored — which is what keeps the guisarme@heavy floor out of danger. FORM SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION, and this is the third scaling term of the session so the reason is named: curvature is DIMENSIONLESS and bounded [0,1], so (1-K*cv) is bounded in [1-K, 1] and cannot tail. Both earlier terms mis-scaled because their inputs were unbounded — S_g carries units (a linear bind differential was dimensionally incoherent) and I_g spans ~1000x (a linear close-quarters multiplier read guandao 48.9).
